title: Deployment priming & ossify thoughts
content:
Quick context:
- Purpose: capture a lightweight, personal checklist and a few hypotheses for "ossifying" a model flip in an environment where clients have sticky sessions and we care about cold-token churn.
- Scope: small-batch flip from model v1.4.2 -> v1.5.0 (quantized variant) for Hosted API region us-west.

High-level goals:
1) Keep 99th pct latency impact < +30ms across synthetic latencies for first 24h.
2) Limit model-quality regression signals: prompt-eval pass rate drop < 0.5% at cohort level.
3) Make rollback trivial: ability to pin client SDK to previous version within 10 minutes.

Key constraints / quirks to remember:
- Some big tenants pin per-tenant model in their profile (tenant-pin API). Those need manual notify and opt-in if we want them on v1.5.
- SDKs have session affinity TTLs (30m) so traffic routing changes will take time to propagate.
- KV-prefix caching behavior: new quantized kernels warm different cache patterns; expect first-token spike for prefix-heavy workloads.

Priming plan (preflip, ~48–72h window):
- Day -3: bake a quantized staging cluster with same HW profile as us-west-hosted. Run smoke generator for 6h with representative seq-length distribution. Capture token-per-request histogram.
- Day -2: run a small cohort of internal clients (10 tenants, low traffic) against v1.5 via opt-in flag. Collect latency/err rate and output-quality diffs (use prompt-suite A/B harness).
- Day -1: KV prewarm job: run a controlled prefix sweep for the top 200 prefixes (from past 7d traffic) to populate KV caches on nodes assigned to v1.5. 2 passes, 30m apart.
- Preflight checklist (T-2h): confirm autoscaler warm targets, confirm fallback model is registered and healthy, prepare feature-flag rollback command, set alert burn-in thresholds.

Canary rollout steps (micro-batch approach):
1) Canary cohort (0.1% traffic) for 30m — watch latency raw and p95/p99, request error rate, anomaly on stop-words hallucination metric.
2) If stable, increase to 1% for 2h across low-latency clients only (client list: internal+beta tenants).
3) 5% for 4h — enable light-weight quality sampling (every 500th request stored & diffed).
4) 20% for 6h with monitoring windows: 10m small-sample checks + hourly full-check.
5) Ramp to 50% overnight if no alerts. Next day, finish to 100% if stable.

Escape hatches and rollback plan:
- Quick pin API: curl -X POST $ADMIN/api/v1/tenants/<TENANT>/pin -d '{"model":"v1.4.2"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
- Global flip rollback: run traffic-router toggle to force old path (doc link: /confluence/infra/traffic-ops), takes ~2m for routing table, but session-TTL means effect completes across ~30m window.
- Hotfix path: if token-spike causes node OOMs, enable smaller max-seq cap and revert to best-effort decoding mode (flag: ENABLE_COMPRESSED_KERNELS=false) while we triage.

Signals to fail fast (auto/manual triggers):
- p99 latency > baseline + 50ms for two consecutive 10m windows.
- Error rate spike > 0.3% absolute and sustained for 15m.
- Eval pass rate drop > 0.75% on safety-critical prompt set.
- Memory pressure across >20% of nodes (OOM events or swap touches).

Lightweight monitoring setup (ops notes):
- Dashboards: per-model p50/p95/p99, token-per-request histogram, mem/swap, evictions-per-minute, cache-hit-rate.
- Alerts: slack #releases + pager on severity for p99/oom. Tag alerts with "ossify-priming" so I can mute during experiments.
- Quick checks: small script to sample 100 in-flight responses and diff against v1.4.2 gold outputs (script path: tools/eval/sample-diff.sh).

Operational gotchas and runbook snippets:
- If a tenant reports quality drift but system metrics look fine: check tenant-pin header and user SDK version — many SDKs will include modelOverride.
- Client-side circuit breakers: some older SDKs will retry aggressively on 429 which can mask latency vs availability issues. Consider enabling soft-429 throttling for the canary window.
- Pre-warm curl probe (run from us-west egress):
  for prefix in $(cat top-prefixes.txt | head -n 50); do
    curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN" -d "{\"prompt\": \"$prefix\"}" >/dev/null &
  done

Open questions / follow ups:
- Are there tenants using per-tenant quantization overrides? Need to ask solutions eng.
- Should we enable cached-response analytics to get better early-warning on hallucination drift? cost vs signal tradeoff.
- Runbook improvement: add a single-click rollback button in Console that pins traffic-router and also nukes per-tenant pin header for specific clients. File a request: https://linear.app/RED/REQ-993

TL;DR checklist (one-liner): bake staging, opt-in beta tenants, KV prewarm top prefixes, micro-canalize 0.1→1→5→20→50→100, watch p99/p95/eval-pass/memory, be ready to pin to v1.4.2 and use routing toggle for global rollback.

Notes to self (freeform):
- Remember to tell comms about possible small spike in 1st-hour CPU; set expectations.
- If we see tiny quality regressions isolated to long-form summarization, try turning on alignment-favors-temperature-reduction flag for those tenants before fully rolling back.
- Postmortem template: include priming steps, prefix-sweep logs, sampled responses, and a timeline of traffic fractions.

End of notes.
